battle.name: 巴比倫對波斯的起義
battle.theater: 底格里斯河畔庫納克薩與巴比倫城
battle.brief: 公元前484年，阿黑美尼德王朝治下的巴比倫與塞種人起兵反抗大流士一世，波斯軍隊在底格里斯河畔的庫納克薩擊潰叛軍，隨後圍困巴比倫，城門開啟後王朝仍以總督取代舊王室。卡面這件亞述長矛早於此役數百年，其形制已融入兩河長矛兵與波斯持盾兵的裝備傳統。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 這場衝突的交戰方分三塊：中央是阿黑美尼德王室的波斯王軍，巴比倫行省是它的前線；巴比倫一方是城邦的城防軍與城外的塞種人聯軍；而周邊行省只是被捲入與徵發的對象。波斯一方由大流士一世在位的帝國構成，國王自稱「大王」，王權以波斯波利斯與蘇薩為核心，另有巴比倫、薩迪斯與埃克巴塔那三座王居，行省總督（波斯語 darbāḵi，亞述—巴比倫傳統稱亞米盧）由國王任免，負責徵稅、徵召兵員與供應王室軍隊。波斯軍隊的骨架是中央王室的常備步兵、弓手與騎兵，戰時再由各行省提供民兵、車乘與糧秣，並僱用外族戰士；御道沿線的驛站與王室快馬構成通訊與指揮的骨架。巴比倫一方是城邦的公民戰士：城牆上的持矛步兵與弓箭手、能出城作戰的步兵方陣，以及塞種人自東北帶來的輕裝騎兵與游騎。塞種人在波斯史料中是一個邊疆族名，與中國文獻的「塞種」可能同源，其出現本身就是這場戰爭的前提。巴比倫的關鍵價值在於它是幼發拉底下游的門戶，控制分汊水道、灌溉渠網與通往波斯灣的海鹽、棕櫚纖維與穀物商路，所以它既是起義的發源地，也是國王必須重新握住的據點。
countriesEn: The belligerents fall into three blocks: at the centre, the Persian royal army of the Achaemenid monarchy, for which Babylonia was a frontier province; on the Babylonian side, the city's defensive forces and the Saka allies coming from outside the walls; and the surrounding provinces, which were only drawn in and levied. The Persian side consisted of the empire under Darius I. The king called himself the Great King, and kingship was centred on Persepolis and Susa, with further royal residences at Babylon, Sardis and Ecbatana. Satraps, in Persian darbāḵi and in the older Assyro-Babylonian usage amilu, were appointed by the king and charged with collecting tribute, mustering troops and supplying the royal army. The backbone of the Persian army was the standing infantry, archers and cavalry of the central household, supplemented in wartime by provincial militia, transport and grain, and by hired foreign fighters; the relay stations of the Royal Road and the royal courier horses formed the skeleton of command and communication. The Babylonian side was the citizen soldiery of a city-state: spearmen and archers on the walls, infantry formations able to fight outside the gates, and the light cavalry and skirmishers the Saka brought down from the north-east. The Saka are a frontier people in the Persian sources, possibly the same people as the Saka of Chinese records, and their appearance is itself a precondition of this war. The value of Babylon lay in its position as the gateway of the lower Euphrates, controlling the split channels, the irrigation network and the sea salt, palm fibre and grain road to the Persian Gulf; it was therefore both the seat of the revolt and the point the king had to win back.
people: 大流士一世是這場戰爭唯一可指名的主角。他在前522年平息加米達之亂後登上王位，靠重整行省、興修御道與宮殿把帝國的財政與軍隊抓回中央，前484年他已統治約三十八年，起義爆發時他的力量正投向歐洲與北疆的戰線。巴比倫編年史把叛軍的領袖記作馬提亞（Martiya，抄本寫法有異），記載他率領城民與塞種人聯軍東進，戰敗後逃往米底，此後再無記載；他是本役唯一留下姓名的叛方人物。另一個在編年史中被提到而姓名不詳的人物是米底的總督，記載稱他被塞種人殺死，他的死亡是巴比倫人敢於起義的直接原因。塞種人首領的名字同樣沒有留下，只知其率部眾自中亞方向進入米底，隨後同巴比倫人合流。巴比倫方面的王族旁支也沒有留下名字：拿波那尼德二世於前539年王朝覆亡時被逐出巴比倫並流亡阿拉伯，其子貝爾伊布尼短暫繼位後被俘，後來的大流士正是靠削弱並吸收這些本地勢力來維持對巴比倫的統治。戰後，巴比倫行省被交給大流士之弟尼布沙那尼拔二世，前479年他出任總督並重建城牆與宮殿，這條線後來接上亞歷山大前331年的征服。相關記述主要來自巴比倫編年史與科提亞斯的《波斯史》，希羅多德與色諾芬都沒有直接記載本役；色諾芬《安納巴asis》所記的庫納克薩之戰屬前401年，是另一場戰爭，只是同名。
peopleEn: Darius I is the only named protagonist of this war. He had taken the throne in 522 BC after settling the Gaumata pretender, and by darning the provinces, opening the Royal Road and building his palaces he had pulled the empire's finances and army back into the centre; by 484 BC he had ruled for about thirty-eight years, and with the revolt breaking out his strength was being committed to the European and northern frontiers. The Babylonian chronicle names the leader of the rebels Martiya, the spellings varying between copies, and records him leading the citizens and the Saka allies out against the Persians and then fleeing to Media after the defeat; he is the only rebel whose name survives. Another person named in the chronicle, whose name is not given, is the satrap of Media, recorded as killed by the Saka, and his death was the immediate reason the Babylonians dared to rise. The name of the Saka chief is not preserved either; only that he led his people into Media from the direction of Central Asia and then joined the Babylonians. No name survives from the Babylonian royal house either. Nabonidus II was driven out of Babylon when the dynasty fell in 539 BC and lived in exile in Arabia; his son Bel-ibni briefly succeeded and was taken prisoner; it was precisely by breaking and absorbing these local forces that Darius held Babylon. After the war the province of Babylonia was handed to Darius's brother Nebuchadnezzar II, who became satrap in 479 BC and rebuilt the walls and the palace; that thread later runs into Alexander's conquest in 331 BC. The account comes chiefly from the Babylonian chronicle and from Ctesias's Persica; neither Herodotus nor Xenophon records this war directly, and the Cunaxa of Xenophon's Anabasis belongs to 401 BC and is a different battle that happens to share the name.
kits: 卡面這件「亞述長矛」屬兩河流域中亞述時期的步兵兵器：短柄、長刃、配著鐵鏃的矛頭，與弓、盾牌是同一名戰士的配備；亞述人正是靠弓矛並用的密集步兵與成熟的攻城技術，把兩河的城市一個接一個打下來。必須說清楚的是，這件兵器並沒有出現在前484年的戰場上：亞述王國在前612至前609年間滅亡，尼尼微與亞述城相繼陷落，亞述的鐵作與工藝傳統散入巴比倫與米底，作為國家象徵的亞述長矛自此只存在於浮雕與後世想像裡。但形制並不隨國家消失。阿黑美尼德波斯步兵的持盾兵（sparabara）使用長矛，長度遠過今日的標槍，配大尺寸的柳條編圓盾（波斯語 gerron）；弓手使用角木皮複合弓與革製箭袋（gorytos），袋中同時收納短弓與箭，箭鏃以燧石、獸骨與銅為多，鐵鏃仍非主流。巴比倫方面的配備與之接近：城防的持矛步兵、牆上的弓箭手，加上可用於近身纏鬥的短刀與彎形匕首；攻城方面，巴比倫與波斯都備有撞槌、覆以濕皮革的攻城塔、可拋擲石塊的投石器，以及在牆下掘地道破壞基礎的做法，這些手段正是埃薩吉拉一帶圍牆被破壞的技術前提。運輸靠牛車、騾馬與人力，軍隊沿幼發拉底兩岸的運河與村鎮取得穀物；就前484年而言，亞述式的長柄兵器在形制上已被更長的波斯長矛取代，但「短柄長刃配鐵鏃再加弓」這一套兩河步兵的組合，仍是理解本役雙方兵器的正確框架。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear on the card belongs to the infantry arm of middle-Assyrian Mesopotamia: a short shaft, a long blade and an iron socketed head, carried together with the bow and the shield by the same man; it was with bow-and-spear infantry in close formation and with siege technique that the Assyrians took the cities of the two rivers one after another. It has to be said plainly that the weapon was not on the field in 484 BC: the Assyrian kingdom had gone out of existence between 612 and 609 BC, Nineveh and Assur having fallen in turn, and the Assyrian ironwork and craft traditions were absorbed by Babylonia and Media, while the Assyrian spear as a state emblem survived only in relief and in later imagination. The form, however, did not die with the state. The Achaemenid Persian shield-bearers, the sparabara, used a long spear far exceeding the length of a modern javelin, together with a large wicker round shield, the Persian gerron; the archers used a composite bow of horn, wood and sinew with a leather quiver, the gorytos, which carried both the short bow and the arrows, the heads being mostly flint, bone and copper, with iron still a minority. The Babylonian equipment was close to this: spearmen on the walls, archers on the parapets, short swords and curved daggers for close work; for siege work both Babylonia and Persia had battering rams, leather-covered towers, stone-throwing engines and the practice of digging under the wall to undermine its foundations, and these means are the technical precondition for the breach of the walls around Esagila. Transport rested on ox carts, mules and human porters, and the army drew grain from the villages and canal network along the Euphrates; for 484 BC the Assyrian long-handled weapon had in form been replaced by the longer Persian spear, but the combination of short shaft, long blade, iron head and bow remained the correct framework for understanding the arms of both sides in this war.
tactics: 波斯軍隊的作戰邏輯是縱隊行軍、集中兵員與騎兵兩翼包抄。從米底方向西進的王軍沿底格里斯河與幼發拉底之間的走廊推進，隊形以縱列拉長，步兵居中，弓手與輕裝騎兵在兩側先行，騎兵負責遮蔽行軍縱列與偵察；一旦接戰，重裝步兵結成密集方陣作正面壓制，兩翼騎兵同時以楔形隊衝擊敵軍側翼與背後，揚起的塵土與馬隊衝撞是這支部隊最有效的破陣手段。前484年春汛之後的作戰多在平原上進行，幼發拉底與底格里斯的水位限制了大規模騎兵在泛濫地帶展開，兩軍的接戰因此傾向於河道之間的高地與道路交會處，庫納克薩的戰場正落在自米底通往巴比倫的這條通道上。巴比倫與塞種的聯軍沒有留下陣形記載，只能按兩河流域的慣例推想：塞種人以輕騎在兩側游擊，避免正面與波斯重裝步兵相撞，巴比倫步兵與弓箭手在正面列陣，一旦正面被騎兵衝垮，陣線很可能在平原上被分割。追擊之後是圍城：波斯軍逼近巴比倫城，封鎖城郊的村鎮、截斷運入城的糧食與水，攻城塔與撞槌同時推到牆下，攻城一段時間後，編年史記載城門開啟。城門開啟之後，報復是節制的：神廟未被焚燒，城市未被拆毀，只有埃薩吉拉一帶的圍牆被破壞，好讓後來的波斯總督能以另一種方式接管這座城。
tacticsEn: The logic of the Persian army was columnar march, concentration of troops and a cavalry envelopment on both flanks. The royal army advancing westward from Media moved along the corridor between the Tigris and the Euphrates, its column drawn out in depth, the infantry in the centre, archers and light cavalry leading on either side, the cavalry screening the marching column and scouting; on contact, the heavy infantry closed into a dense formation for frontal pressure while the cavalry on both wings charged in wedge to strike the flanks and the rear of the enemy, and the dust and the mass of horses were the most effective means of breaking a line. Campaigning in 484 BC fell in the plain after the spring flood, and the levels of the Euphrates and the Tigris limited the deployment of massed cavalry on the inundated ground, so contact tended to be made on the higher ground and at the crossroads of the roads between the two rivers; the field of Cunaxa lay exactly on that corridor running from Media to Babylon. No record survives of the order of battle of the Babylonian and Saka alliance, and it can only be inferred from the habits of the two rivers: the Saka would skirmish with light cavalry on the flanks, avoiding a frontal collision with the Persian heavy infantry, while Babylonian infantry and archers formed up in front, and once the front was broken by a cavalry charge the line was likely to be cut apart on the open plain. The next stage was the siege: the Persian army closed on Babylon, sealed the villages around it, cut off the food and water coming in, and brought towers and rams up to the walls; after a period of siege the chronicle records that the gates were opened. What followed the opening of the gates was restrained: the temples were not burned, the city was not levelled, and only the walls around Esagila were broken, so that a later Persian satrap could take the city over in a different manner.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。時間一類最確定：大流士一世在位前522至前486年，起義發生在他的第十三年，即巴比倫編年史的「大流士二年」，換算為公元前484年；拿波那尼德二世於前539年亡國，尼布沙那尼拔二世則於前479年出任巴比倫總督。地理一類：巴比倫城在幼發拉底東岸、今伊拉克中部，庫納克薩一般定位在巴比倫以北數十公里、底格里斯河左岸一帶，兩地之間沒有可靠里數，但都在同一天然的行軍走廊上；希羅多德描述巴比倫城為方形，牆體每邊約十五斯塔德，全城周圍約六十斯塔德，牆高以肘計；現代測量則給出內城面積約一百公頃，內外城牆合計周長約十八公里，兩組數字反映的是同時代觀察與今日殘跡的不同尺度。軍力一類沒有可靠數字：巴比倫編年史只說叛軍眾多，波斯方面也不留下人數，王軍的組成可從常備、行省民兵與僱傭兵三部分推想，數量本身無從核實。物資方面可以說的是，前五世紀的箭鏃仍以燧石、獸骨與銅為主流，鐵多用於矛頭與近身兵器；波斯浮雕所見的箭袋一囊約容三十支箭；巴比倫城郊與幼發拉底兩岸的運河村落，是圍城期間補給的主要來源，圍城的實際長度無記載，推測為數週至數月。整場起義從爆發到城破，編年史只以年計，跨度當在一年之內。
dataEn: The checkable numbers fall into three classes. The first is time, and it is the firmest: Darius I reigned from 522 to 486 BC, so the revolt broke out in his thirteenth year, which is the second year of Darius in the Babylonian chronicle, converting to 484 BC; Nabonidus II's kingdom ended in 539 BC, and Nebuchadnezzar II became satrap of Babylonia in 479 BC. The second class is geography: Babylon stood on the east bank of the Euphrates in what is now central Iraq, while Cunaxa is generally placed some dozens of kilometres north of the city on the left bank of the Tigris; there is no reliable figure for the distance between them, but both lie on the same natural corridor of march. Herodotus describes Babylon as a square city, each side about fifteen stades, the whole circuit about sixty stades, the height of the wall given in cubits; modern survey gives the inner city at about a hundred hectares and the combined circuit of the inner and outer walls at about eighteen kilometres, the two sets of figures reflecting the difference between a contemporary observation and the scale of today's remains. The third class, the strength of the armies, has no reliable figures at all: the Babylonian chronicle says only that the rebels were numerous, Persia left no numbers either, and the composition of the royal army can be inferred as standing troops, provincial militia and mercenaries, but the quantity itself cannot be checked. What can be said of materiel is that in the fifth century BC arrowheads were still mainly flint, bone and copper, with iron used for spearheads and close-quarter arms; the quivers shown in Persian relief hold about thirty arrows each; the villages and canal settlements around Babylon and along the Euphrates were the main source of supply during the siege, and the actual length of the siege is unrecorded, probably weeks to a few months. From the outbreak of the revolt to the fall of the city the chronicle counts only in years, and the span must have fallen within a single year.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層，可以由外而內。最外一層是塞種人自中亞方向進入米底並在米底造成崩潰：編年史記載米底的王被塞種人殺死，說明這不是邊境的小股掠奪，而是足以摧毀一個行省統治中樞的深入行動。亞述人與巴比倫人的後裔中，帝國的邊疆從來是靠行省總督、僱傭兵與驃騎反覆守住的，一旦出現這種規模的入侵，王室必須把大批兵馬調去北方，南方行省的守備與監視就會鬆動。第二層是阿黑美尼德中央集權對巴比倫的抽取：大流士把行省稅收、軍隊徵召與御道驛站統一到王室，巴比倫的城邦經濟、地方菁英與神廟財產都被納入這套體系，繳納的一方是本地菁英，收穫的是王室；王位合法性同樣是一個變數，拿波那尼德一系被逐與被俘之後，巴比倫的政治氛圍裡存在對「王位該由誰來坐」的期待。第三層是塞種入侵與巴比倫起義在同一時刻合流：塞種人從米底方向南下，威脅到巴比倫的北面與幼發拉底交通線，兩河流域的形勢使巴比倫的守軍、主祭與商團同時相信可以趁亂脫離波斯的控制，於是叛旗在城內豎起。對波斯國王而言，鎮壓這場起義不是懲罰一座城，而是要證明行省的體系能撐住一次內部衝擊。
causeEn: There are three layers to the reason the fighting began, from the outside in. The outermost is the Saka entering Media from the direction of Central Asia and bringing collapse there: the chronicle records that the king of Media was killed by the Saka, which shows this was not a small border raid but an incursion deep enough to destroy the seat of a provincial administration. Among the successors of the Assyrians and Babylonians, the empire's frontier had always been held by satraps, mercenaries and mounted riders turned back again and again, and once an incursion of this scale appeared the court had to move large bodies of troops north, which loosened the guard and the surveillance of the southern provinces. The second layer is the extraction exerted by Achaemenid centralisation on Babylon: Darius brought provincial tribute, military mustering and the relay stations of the Royal Road under royal control, and the economy of the city, the local elite and the temple estates were all drawn into that system, with the local elite paying and the court collecting; legitimacy of kingship was a variable as well, and after the banishment and capture of the Nabonidus line there was an expectation in Babylon about who ought to occupy the throne. The third layer is that the Saka incursion and the Babylonian revolt came together at the same moment: the Saka came south out of Media, threatening northern Babylonia and the traffic of the Euphrates, and the conditions in Mesopotamia made the garrison, the chief priest and the merchant community of Babylon all believe that the city could break free while the empire was off balance, so the banner of revolt was raised inside the walls. For the king of Persia, putting down the revolt was not the punishment of a city but the proof that the provincial system could survive an internal shock.
impact: 這場起義的後果首先落在巴比倫的行政上。城破之後，帝國沒有像前689年薩那赫里布那樣把巴比倫連根拔起，而是保留城市、神廟與神像，把巴比倫從城邦改為王室的直轄行省，任命總督管理，並以常駐守軍與不斷的糧秣維持城防；巴比倫人自己曾為大流士立像，銘文以「大流士王，建造巴比倫城者」相稱，這尊像把征服者寫成城市的恩主，是波斯統治合法性最直接的一次公開操作。前479年，大流士把巴比倫行省交給其弟尼布沙那尼拔二世，後者重建城牆與宮殿，巴比倫自此在波斯體系中的地位高於一般行省，並一直是東方的支柱，直到前331年被亞歷山大佔領。軍事的教訓同樣被記取：塞種人之役之後，波斯在北疆的用兵明顯加強，希羅多德記載大流士在前519年再度征討塞種並擒其首，離開波斯的薛西斯在前480年入侵希臘時也把戰線拉過米底與亞美尼亞，底格里斯河上的渡河點與軍道因而成為帝國北部的常設關切。對兩河流域的城邦居民而言，這場起義幾乎被編年史壓縮成幾行，但它說明一件事：阿黑美尼德王室的行省體系有能力在最不利的時候守住幼發拉底下游，而城邦自身的傳統軍制並不足以單獨承擔這一任務。
impactEn: The consequences of the revolt first fell on the administration of Babylon. After the city fell, the empire did not tear Babylon out by the roots as Sennacherib had done in 689 BC, but kept the city, its temples and its images, converted Babylon from a city-state into a province under the crown, appointed a satrap to govern it, and maintained the walls with a garrison and a regular flow of supplies; the Babylonians themselves set up a statue of Darius, the inscription calling him the king who built the city of Babylon, and that statue turned the conqueror into a benefactor in public, the most direct public operation of Persian legitimacy ever carried out. In 479 BC Darius handed the province of Babylonia to his brother Nebuchadnezzar II, who rebuilt the walls and the palace, and from then on Babylon stood above an ordinary province within the Persian system and remained a pillar of the east until Alexander took it in 331 BC. The military lesson was equally taken to heart: after the war with the Saka the empire's northern operations grew visibly more persistent, Herodotus has Darius campaigning against the Saka again in 519 BC and taking their chief, and Xerxes on his departure from Persia in 480 BC drew the line of his invasion of Greece back through Media and Armenia, so the crossing places of the Tigris and the military roads became a standing concern of the empire's northern frontier. For the city populations of Mesopotamia the revolt is compressed to a few lines in the Mesopotamian chronicle, yet it shows one thing clearly: the Achaemenid provincial system was able to hold the lower Euphrates at the worst possible moment, and the civic military institutions of a city-state were not by themselves enough to bear that task.
result: 結果可以分為已確定的部分與只能推測的部分。已確定的有四點：其一，塞種人攻入米底並殺死米底的王，北疆的崩潰先於巴比倫的叛旗；其二，巴比倫人起兵並與塞種人合流，叛軍在巴比倫以北的戰場上被波斯軍隊擊潰，馬提亞率殘部逃往米底，此後再無記載；其三，波斯軍隊隨即包圍巴比倫，城門在圍城一段時間之後開啟，城市落入國王軍隊之手，編年史記載埃薩吉拉一帶的圍牆被破壞；其四，起義被平定，但巴比倫並未被焚毀或拆平，祭祀與神像維持，帝國改以總督直轄該地，再於前479年把行省交給尼布沙那尼拔二世重建。只能推測的部分是戰役的細節：聯軍的具體陣形、攻城器械的數量、圍城的實際月數，以及城破後叛軍首腦的處置方式，都沒有留下可靠記載。評價上，多數研究者把前484年視為一次規模有限但真實存在的行省叛亂，而不是一場大規模戰爭；它同時是伊朗史料傳統中「塞種戰爭」的一環，在那裡帶有劫後重建與邊疆記憶的雙重分量。對亞述—巴比倫—波斯這條長線而言，本役最值得記住的是：這是巴比倫以城邦形式挑戰帝國的少數幾次之一，而它以失敗與一次徹底的行政重組告終。
resultEn: The outcome divides into what is established and what can only be inferred. Four things are established. First, the Saka penetrated Media and killed the king of Media, so the collapse of the northern frontier came before the banner of revolt in Babylon. Second, the Babylonians rose and joined the Saka, and the allied rebel force was destroyed by the Persian army in the field north of the city, Martiya escaping with the remnants to Media, after which no trace of him remains. Third, the Persian army at once invested Babylon, the gates were opened after a period of siege, the city passed into the hands of the king's troops, and the chronicle records that the walls around Esagila were broken. Fourth, the revolt was put down, but Babylon was neither burned nor razed: the sacrifices and the images were maintained, the empire ruled the place directly through a satrap, and in 479 BC handed the province to Nebuchadnezzar II to rebuild. Only the details of the campaign have to be inferred: the order of battle of the allies, the number of siege engines, the actual months of the siege, and the disposal of the rebel leaders are not reliably recorded. In assessment, most researchers treat 484 BC as a provincial revolt of limited scale but genuine, rather than as a great war; it is at the same time one of the Saka wars of Iranian historical tradition, where it carries a double weight of survival and frontier memory. For the long line running through Assyria, Babylon and Persia, the thing most worth remembering about this war is that it is one of the few occasions on which Babylon challenged an empire in its civic form, and it ended in defeat and in a thorough administrative reconstruction.
